title: from different generations
intro: When you were younger, did you have a special bond with your grandparents? Many of us develop particularly close attachments with older family members, but did you know that this ability for the oldest and youngest of our society to get along in a friendly way is not limited to families? In fact, there are some projects which pair together nurseries and retirement homes, to help reduce feelings of loneliness and improve everybody's general health and happiness. Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary.
this_week_question: What generation would someone born in 1982 be in?
a) Generation X b) Millennial c) Gen Z
Listen to the programme to hear the answer.

vocab.desc: group of people who are of a similar age fill a void help to feel better after experiencing loss such and such reference to something without giving a specific example hear on the grapevine hear a rumour break down stereotypes find evidence that common beliefs about a group of people are untrue lively loud and with lots of energy

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Hi Georgie.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Hi Phil.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: So, Georgie, do you often spend time with people who are much older than you or much younger than you?

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: I do, actually, because I'm in a choir, so there's quite a wide range of ages – lots of older people, lots of younger people.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: We can call an age group of people a generation . And you might feel that it's difficult to understand or agree with people from a different generation . Today on 6 Minute English, we're going to be finding out about a project that is gathering together the oldest people – that's those that are retired – with the youngest, and that's children who attend nursery. And we'll be asking the question, 'What can we learn from different generations ?'

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie. What generation would someone born in 1982 be in? Is it: a)    Generation X, b)    Millennial, or c)    Gen Z.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Phil, I'm going to go with Generation X.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: OK. Well, we will find out the answer at the end of the programme.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: OK. Phil, so you said we're going to look at a project which gets small children interacting with older retired people. So, how does it work?

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Well, in Chester, in the northwest of England, a nursery has opened up in a retirement village. There's the usual nursery staff to look after the children, but the older residents can join in for activities as well. There's a library, a cafeteria and a garden for the children and the older people to share, and some of the older people or 'grand-friends', as the children call them, lead some of the activities, like dance or crafts. And presenter of BBC World Service podcast People Fixing the World, Myra Anubi, went to visit the special nursery and spoke to some of the participants.

transcript.author: Myra Anubi
transcript.text: Ian was once a fighter pilot, and getting involved in the nursery has helped him fill a void .

transcript.author: Ian
transcript.text: It was after my wife died last year. It seemed I had a big, big hole to fill. And the people down in the nursery, they phoned me up and said, "We were doing such and such a thing. Why don't you come and join us?" And that's what I've been doing. So, yes, and I've enjoyed it. And I find it very interesting to see how they develop.

transcript.author: Myra Anubi
transcript.text: One of the things I heard from the grapevine is that you help the children make paper planes.

transcript.author: Ian
transcript.text: That's right.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Myra says that the nursery helped Ian fill a void after his wife sadly died. If you fill a void , you find something to help you feel better after a loss.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Ian explains that after his wife died, staff at the nursery would phone him to tell him about the daily activities, which he refers to as such and such . And that's an expression that we use to talk about something without giving a specific example.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: It sounds like Ian has enjoyed spending time with the children at the nursery, and Myra tells him she's heard from the grapevine that he's been teaching the children to make paper planes.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Yes, hear from the grapevine is an expression, meaning that something is a rumour. And we also say, hear on the grapevine .

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Well, this nursery sounds like a really lovely project, Phil. What is the impact it's having on the older and younger people?

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Well, the charity Ready Generations, which runs the nursery, says it works with universities to study the effects of mixing generations on health and wellbeing, and they say they've seen positive results. And there have been studies around the world on projects that encourage different generations to mix, and they found that they can help reduce loneliness, improve how healthy and well people feel, and even boost learning and creativity. People Fixing the World host Myra spoke to Liz Ludden, co-founder of the nursery in Chester, about the differences that she's noticed since it opened.

transcript.author: Myra Anubi
transcript.text: And as I realised, these interactions also seem to be breaking down stereotypes .

transcript.author: Liz Ludden
transcript.text: Your first thought would be how lively and energetic young children can be, and what we found is so can older people. And so sometimes, you know, it's the older people that we're saying, "Can we just calm this down a little bit?"

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Myra says the nursery breaks down stereotypes . This means it provides evidence that common beliefs about a group of people are not true.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: For example, a stereotype about generations is that younger people are lively , meaning they're loud and have lots of energy, whereas older people are not that lively .

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Right. But in the nursery, Liz says it's often the older people who have lots of energy and are being noisy rather than the children. The staff even have to tell them to calm down sometimes!

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: So, Georgie, is that something that you found in your choir?

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Actually, yes. The older people in my choir are big characters. It's often them who are dragging us all to the pub...!

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: OK. Georgie, I think it's time to look at the answer for that question. I asked if someone was born in 1982, which generation would they be from?

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: I said Generation X.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: OK. Well, actually, I'm afraid the answer was b) – they're a Millennial, just like you!

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Ah...! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with generation , which is a group of people who are of a similar age.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Fill a void means find something to help you feel better after experiencing loss.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Such and such is a way to talk about something without giving a specific example.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: If you hear something on the grapevine , you hear a rumour.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: The expression break down stereotypes means find evidence that common beliefs about a group of people are untrue.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: And lively means loud and with lots of energy.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website. Go to bbclearningenglish.com.

transcript.author: Phil
transcript.text: Thanks for joining us and goodbye.

transcript.author: Georgie
transcript.text: Goodbye!
